title: Prohibition of Alcohol in Islam
summary: Alcohol consumption is strictly prohibited in Islam by Quran and Hadith.
translation: Drinking alcohol is prohibited, with its prohibition rooted in both the Quran and the Hadith. Thus, there is no justification for its consumption under any circumstances. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said—narrated by Abdullah bin Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)—that he forbade the drinking of alcohol and gambling. He stated that anything causing intoxication is also forbidden. Furthermore, in another Hadith, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said that those who unjustly disobey their parents, habitually gamble, boast about charity given to the poor, or regularly consume alcohol will not enter Paradise. From this, it is clear that the Prophet (peace be upon him) strongly forbade Muslims from drinking, using, promoting, or engaging with alcohol in any way. Therefore, anyone involved with alcohol, in any form, should heed the Prophet's words, repent, and lead a life avoiding these sins. Allah sent Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a mercy to the world, who said in a Hadith that Allah, with His honor, has sworn that anyone who drinks even a drop of alcohol will be made to drink as much pus of Hell-dwellers, but for anyone who forgoes alcohol out of fear of Allah, He will let them drink pure beverages from the rivers of Paradise. Therefore, it's understood that alcohol is absolutely forbidden, incurring the displeasure of Allah and the Prophet (peace be upon him). We must completely repent from alcohol, advise those who drink to stop, and avoid incurring Allah's wrath, leading a life free from such vices.
